decision: Split rlsentry into a chain; first task is anon-probe (live black-box scan with anon key)
why: The request is a whole product; the black-box probe is what directly answers "verification, not reminders" and fixes the verdict/report model the rest builds on

decision: Write probe on by default but must never persist a row; uncertain → verdict unknown
why: Write exposure is half the CVE; scanning real prod data makes persistence the worst-case failure

decision: Reports never contain row values, only table, columns, row count
why: Exposed rows are likely third-party PII and reports land in CI logs

decision: No service-role key accepted in this task
why: Scan must see exactly what an outsider sees; avoids handling a secret

decision: Write probe: constraint-violation inference first, Prefer tx=rollback fallback, insert-then-delete forbidden
why: Owner chose A+B from the three options; C can leave rows in production when anon can insert but not delete

decision: Scope of first task confirmed: anon role, one live project, REST tables only
Rebased task/anon-probe onto origin/main (was cut from stale local main lacking harness setup)
why: Branch must start from current main

decision: Spiked RLS ordering in plain Postgres 16 instead of PostgREST
why: Docker Hub rate-limited (429); downloading the PostgREST binary was denied by the session's permission classifier; PostgREST facts P1-P4 left to the first ticket

decision: Method A confirmed sound for insert and update: WITH CHECK runs before constraints
why: 42501 vs 23502 observed for every policy shape tried

decision: Found two limits that conflict with the brief: pk-filling triggers let the probe row persist (S-4); value-based policies make blank-row rejection a false 'protected' (S-5)
why: Observed rows persisted (t_trig, t_trig2) and value policy accepted (t_owner)

decision: Only write_probe may send mutating requests; report type has no field for row values
why: One owner for mutation and a structural guarantee for S-6
